tfResources.role: primary/only mapped resource — 1:1 equivalent of CfnHttpNamespace; TF resource ServiceDiscoveryHttpNamespaceConfig covers name, description, and tags directly with no nested sub-resources required

attributeNotes: CfnHttpNamespaceProps fields (verified against servicediscovery.generated.d.ts lines 89-110): description (optional string) maps directly to TF `description` (optional string) — no casing/shape difference. name (required string) maps directly to TF `name` (required string). tags (optional Array<cdk.CfnTag>, i.e. a list of {key, value} objects) maps to TF `tags`, which is a flat map `{[key: string]: string}` rather than a list of key/value objects — requires reshaping CfnTag[] into a Record<string,string> during conversion (and CFN's list form technically allows duplicate keys, which the TF map form cannot). No unmappable Cfn props: description, name, and tags are all covered. Read-only Cfn attributes attrArn and attrId (generated.d.ts lines 41, 47) map to TF computed attributes `arn` and `id` respectively. The TF resource exposes additional fields with no Cfn equivalent — `region` (optional, provider-configurable AWS region), the settable `id` (also computed), `http_name` (computed, informational), and `tags_all` (Terraform/AWS-provider merged tags) — all additive/provider-specific, not a props mismatch. CfnHttpNamespaceProps has no nested/embedded Cfn resource structures, so this remains a strict one-to-one mapping. The `data-aws-service-discovery-http-namespace` directory is a read-only data source, not a create-side mapping target, and was correctly excluded.

tfResources.role: primary/sole mapped resource — covers name, description, tags (tags_all is provider-managed aggregate, not a Cfn prop); exposes computed attr `arn` (maps to CfnPublicDnsNamespace.attrArn) and `hosted_zone` (maps to attrHostedZoneId — confirmed in existing repo usage at src/aws/edge/cloudmap/public-dns-namespace.ts:122, `this.namespaceHostedZoneId = this.resource.hostedZone`). Terraform resource id itself serves as the equivalent of attrId.

attributeNotes:
Verified against CFN servicediscovery.generated.d.ts (CfnPublicDnsNamespace at lines 426-546, CfnPublicDnsNamespaceProps at 556-584) and TF service-discovery-public-dns-namespace/index.d.ts (provider aws 6.52.0). Confirmed via `ls .../lib | grep -i service-discovery`: only service-discovery-public-dns-namespace is relevant (service-discovery-private-dns-namespace, -http-namespace, -service, -instance are for other Cfn resources/services; data-aws-* are read-only data sources, not applicable here).

Cfn -> TF field mapping:
- description -> description (direct, optional string). CONFIRMED both sides.
- name -> name (direct, required string). CONFIRMED both sides.
- tags (Array<CfnTag> {Key,Value}) -> tags (TF map<string,string>). CONFIRMED: TF config declares tags as `{ [key: string]: string }`; Cfn tagsRaw is Array<cdk.CfnTag>. Shape/casing mismatch: Cfn tags are a list of {Key,Value} objects, TF tags is a flat Terraform map; keys/values are semantically equivalent but structurally different and must be converted list<->map.
- properties.dnsProperties.soa.ttl (number, SOA record negative-caching TTL, seconds) -> UNMAPPABLE. CONFIRMED: the Cfn nesting is CfnPublicDnsNamespace.PropertiesProperty (line 510) -> dnsProperties: PublicDnsPropertiesMutableProperty (line 525) -> soa: SOAProperty (line 540) -> ttl?: number (line 546). The `aws_service_discovery_public_dns_namespace` TF resource (6.52.0) exposes no `properties`/`dns_properties`/`soa` argument at all (config has only description, id, name, region, tags, tagsAll) — there is no way to set the SOA TTL for a public DNS namespace via this TF resource/provider version. This is a genuine capability gap, not a naming mismatch. Handling: drop/ignore this prop during conversion (or emit a warning/TODO comment in generated code); if the SOA TTL value truly must be enforced, it would require an out-of-band call (e.g. AWS CLI/SDK `update-public-dns-namespace` or a Route 53 hosted-zone SOA record tweak) outside of Terraform, which is out of scope for a direct resource mapping.
- Top-level `properties` (CfnPublicDnsNamespace.PropertiesProperty wrapper struct) itself has no TF equivalent beyond the unmapped soa.ttl leaf — the wrapper struct disappears entirely since TF flattens SOA support out.
- Cfn readonly attributes: attrArn (line 451) -> TF `arn` (direct); attrHostedZoneId (line 457) -> TF `hosted_zone` (name/casing differs: HostedZoneId vs hosted_zone, camel/PascalCase CFN attr vs snake_case TF computed attribute); attrId (line 463) -> TF logical resource `id` (the Terraform resource's own `id` attribute serves this role, no separate exported field named `Id`).
- TF-only extras with no Cfn counterpart: `region` (provider/region override — infra-level knob), `tags_all` (merged provider-default + resource tags, a TF/provider computed convenience field), `id` as a settable input (import-only edge case per TF docs footnote, not a real Cfn analog).
- No CDK `PublicDnsNamespaceProps` (L2) fields such as SOA TTL surface at Cfn/TF layer beyond what's listed above; the L2 construct wraps the same Cfn resource 1:1 with defaults. (Note: public DNS namespaces have no vpc-scoping — vpc is a PrivateDnsNamespace-only concept, correctly absent here.)

tfResources.role: Primary 1:1 equivalent. Maps CfnPrivateDnsNamespaceProps.name -> name, .description -> description, .vpc -> vpc, .tags -> tags (map). Computed attrs align: attrArn -> arn, attrHostedZoneId -> hostedZone, attrId -> id (namespace ID, also the import id).

attributeNotes:
Verified against /Users/vincentsmet/tcons/conversion-run/cdklib/node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/aws-servicediscovery/lib/servicediscovery.generated.d.ts (CfnPrivateDnsNamespaceProps props description/name/properties/tags/vpc; nested PropertiesProperty/PrivateDnsPropertiesMutableProperty/SOAProperty; class attrs attrArn/attrHostedZoneId/attrId at lines 270/276/282) and /Users/vincentsmet/tcons/base-servicediscovery-run5/node_modules/@cdktn/provider-aws/lib/service-discovery-private-dns-namespace/index.d.ts (ServiceDiscoveryPrivateDnsNamespaceConfig + class getters), provider aws 6.52.0.

Directly mapped:
- name (required string) -> name (required string). Match.
- description (optional string) -> description (optional string). Match.
- vpc (required string, VPC ID) -> vpc (required string, VPC ID). Match.
- tags (Array<cdk.CfnTag> i.e. [{key,value}, ...]) -> tags ({[key:string]:string} map). Structural transform required: CFN list of Key/Value objects -> TF flat string map, key-by-key (tagKey -> mapKey, tagValue -> mapValue). No functional loss.

Unmappable Cfn prop (zero hits grepping the TF resource dir for soa/dnsProperties/dns_properties):
- properties?: cdk.IResolvable | PropertiesProperty -> { dnsProperties?: { soa?: { ttl?: number } } }. Sets the negative-caching TTL on the SOA record of the Route 53 private hosted zone Cloud Map auto-creates. aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace exposes no equivalent argument, and no sibling service-discovery-* TF resource covers it. Handling: drop/ignore on conversion (or flag as manual follow-up). Modifying SOA TTL out-of-band via aws_route53_zone is not directly possible because the zone is implicitly managed by Cloud Map, not by a TF-managed route53_zone tied to this namespace. A non-default SOA TTL in the source template is silently unrepresentable in the current provider surface.

Computed/attribute mapping (read-only getters on the TF resource):
- attrArn -> get arn(): string. Match.
- attrHostedZoneId -> get hostedZone(): string. Match (casing differs; semantically the Route53 hosted zone ID).
- attrId -> get id(): string (also generateConfigForImport importFromId). Match — both are the Cloud Map namespace ID.

TF-only fields with no CFN source (no data loss, informational): region? (meta arg, defaults to provider region), tagsAll ({[key:string]:string} computed, provider default_tags merge), and an optional passthrough id input. None correspond to a CFN prop; none drop any CFN intent.

Other service-discovery-* dirs (service-discovery-http-namespace, service-discovery-instance, service-discovery-public-dns-namespace, service-discovery-service, data-aws-service-discovery-*) were reviewed and are NOT applicable — they map to other Cfn resources (CfnHttpNamespace, CfnInstance, CfnPublicDnsNamespace, CfnService) or are read-only data sources. Clean 1-to-1 mapping (oneToMany=false); the only nested Cfn sub-property (PropertiesProperty/SOA) is simply unsupported by the provider rather than represented as its own resource.

tfResources.role: Primary/sole mapping. All nested Cfn complex-type props (DnsConfigProperty, DnsRecordProperty, HealthCheckConfigProperty, HealthCheckCustomConfigProperty) are represented as nested blocks/attributes within this single TF resource (dns_config { dns_records { ... } }, health_check_config { ... }, health_check_custom_config { ... }) — they are NOT separate standalone TF resources, so this is a 1:1 (not one-to-many) resource mapping. VERIFIED against index.d.ts: ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig carries dnsConfig/healthCheckConfig/healthCheckCustomConfig as inline nested interfaces (ServiceDiscoveryServiceDnsConfig, ServiceDiscoveryServiceHealthCheckConfig, ServiceDiscoveryServiceHealthCheckCustomConfig), each rendered as its own OutputReference ComplexObject — no separate TerraformResource classes exist for them.

attributeNotes:
Field-by-field mapping, CfnServiceProps -> ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig (VERIFIED against aws-cdk-lib servicediscovery.generated.d.ts and @cdktn/provider-aws service-discovery-service/index.d.ts, provider aws 6.52.0):
- description -> description (direct, string; both optional). VERIFIED.
- name -> name (direct, string). VERIFIED strictness mismatch: TF `name` is REQUIRED (ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig.name has no `?`, line 26) whereas CFN `Name` is optional (CfnServiceProps.name?, and CfnService constructor props are themselves optional — constructor(props?: CfnServiceProps)); CFN can autogenerate the name. During conversion a name value must be supplied to satisfy the TF interface even when the CFN source omitted it (AWS API itself may still generate one, but CDKTF's required typing forces a value in config).
- namespaceId -> namespaceId (direct, string) at the TOP level. Both optional (CFN CfnServiceProps.namespaceId?, TF top-level ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig.namespaceId? — line 30, optional/resettable). NOTE: CFN docs say namespaceId may be an ID or ARN (cross-account shared namespace); TF's namespace_id is documented primarily as a plain namespace ID — verify shared-namespace/ARN support before relying on it (possible loss of ARN capability).
- dnsConfig (CfnService.DnsConfigProperty | IResolvable, optional) -> dnsConfig (ServiceDiscoveryServiceDnsConfig, optional), nested block, camelCase in the CDKTF TS layer (maps to snake_case dns_config in HCL/JSON).
  - dnsConfig.dnsRecords (Array<DnsRecordProperty|IResolvable>|IResolvable, REQUIRED within DnsConfig) -> dnsConfig.dnsRecords (ServiceDiscoveryServiceDnsConfigDnsRecords[]|IResolvable, REQUIRED — line 132, no `?`). Both required. Same shape.
    - DnsRecordProperty.ttl (number, seconds, REQUIRED) -> dnsRecords[].ttl (number, REQUIRED — line 76) — direct, same unit.
    - DnsRecordProperty.type (string, REQUIRED) -> dnsRecords[].type (string, REQUIRED — line 80) — direct.
  - dnsConfig.namespaceId (optional string in CFN, docs mark deprecated: "Use NamespaceId in Service instead") -> dnsConfig.namespaceId (REQUIRED string in TF — line 122, no `?`). VERIFIED MISMATCH: CFN makes this optional/deprecated at the nested-DnsConfig level (top-level namespaceId preferred), but TF's ServiceDiscoveryServiceDnsConfig.namespaceId is required — conversion must always populate it (typically the same value as the top-level namespace_id) whenever a dns_config block is emitted, even though CFN treats it as legacy/optional.
  - dnsConfig.routingPolicy (optional string) -> dnsConfig.routingPolicy (optional string — line 126, resettable) — direct.
- healthCheckConfig (HealthCheckConfigProperty|IResolvable, optional) -> healthCheckConfig (ServiceDiscoveryServiceHealthCheckConfig, optional), nested block; three sub-fields:
  - failureThreshold (optional number) -> failureThreshold (optional number — line 163) — direct.
  - resourcePath (optional string) -> resourcePath (optional string — line 167) — direct.
  - type (CFN: REQUIRED string within HealthCheckConfigProperty) -> type (TF: OPTIONAL string — line 171, `type?`) — VERIFIED strictness mismatch: CFN requires `Type` whenever HealthCheckConfigProperty is supplied; TF exposes it optional (defaults per AWS API). Functionally compatible; carry the CFN value through.
- healthCheckCustomConfig (HealthCheckCustomConfigProperty|IResolvable, optional) -> healthCheckCustomConfig (ServiceDiscoveryServiceHealthCheckCustomConfig, optional), nested block:
  - failureThreshold (optional number; CFN docs: "no longer supported and is always set to 1") -> failureThreshold (optional number — line 204) — direct. Per AWS docs the value is effectively fixed at 1 on both sides; safe to omit or set to 1. NOTE: CFN's HealthCheckCustomConfigProperty has ONLY this one field (failureThreshold) — VERIFIED, matches TF's single-field ServiceDiscoveryServiceHealthCheckCustomConfig.
- tags (Array<CfnTag> — list of {key,value} objects) -> tags (TF: map<string,string> {[key:string]:string} — lines 40-42) — VERIFIED SHAPE MISMATCH: CFN tags is a list of Key/Value objects, TF tags is a flat string map; must transform list-of-{Key,Value} into a Record<string,string> during conversion. TF also exposes a computed tagsAll (merged provider default_tags + tags — lines 46-48) with no CFN equivalent — informational/computed, not user-settable input.
- type (optional string, e.g. "HTTP" for HTTP-namespace-only, no-DNS-record services) -> type (optional string — line 52) — direct.
- serviceAttributes (any | IResolvable — arbitrary key/value map of custom service attributes) -> UNMAPPABLE. VERIFIED: no corresponding attribute exists on ServiceDiscoveryServiceConfig (nor on data-aws-service-discovery-service, which is read-only). CloudFormation-only convenience property with no Terraform AWS provider equivalent as of provider v6.52.0. Handling: drop during conversion and flag/warn (data loss); no other CDKTF-provider-aws resource exposes ServiceAttributes for aws_service_discovery_service.
- TF-ONLY fields with no CFN CfnServiceProps equivalent (leave unset / not sourced from CFN): forceDestroy (boolean|IResolvable, optional — line 15; TF-specific delete behavior), region (string, optional — line 36; TF provider-level region override), and id (string, optional — line 22; the auto-added SDK meta id field). These are Terraform-side conveniences/meta-args, not CFN inputs; no mapping needed.
- Cfn-only outputs (not props, relevant to full fidelity): Arn, Id, InstanceCount, Name are CFN Fn::GetAtt/Ref return values (attrArn, attrId, attrName on CfnService); TF resource exposes equivalent computed attributes automatically (arn via getter line 244, id, etc.) — no explicit config mapping needed, just referenced differently (resource.arn vs Fn::GetAtt). Note: CFN exposes InstanceCount as a GetAtt; the TF aws_service_discovery_service resource does not surface a computed instance_count attribute (minor read-only fidelity gap, not a config input).
- Considered but NOT part of this mapping: aws_service_discovery_http_namespace / aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace / aws_service_discovery_public_dns_namespace correspond to the separate CfnHttpNamespace/CfnPrivateDnsNamespace/CfnPublicDnsNamespace CFN resources (namespaceId input), not to CfnService itself — only relevant when resolving the namespaceId reference chain, out of scope for CfnService's own prop mapping. Similarly aws_service_discovery_instance corresponds to CfnInstance, not CfnService.

cfnResource: AWS::ServiceDiscovery::Instance (CfnInstance / CfnInstanceProps, from aws-cdk-lib aws-servicediscovery v2.233.0 — used internally by L2 constructs alias-target-instance.ts, cname-instance.ts, ip-instance.ts, non-ip-instance.ts)

tfResources.role: primary — sole mapped resource; 1:1 with CfnInstance, no nested/standalone sub-resources are spun off

attributeNotes:
CfnInstanceProps has exactly three props, all of which map directly (verified against servicediscovery.generated.d.ts lines 174-235 and service-discovery-instance/index.d.ts lines 7-35):
- instanceAttributes (any | IResolvable, required, key/value map of AWS_* attribute names) -> ServiceDiscoveryInstanceConfig.attributes ({[key:string]:string}, required). Same semantics (AWS_INSTANCE_IPV4, AWS_INSTANCE_IPV6, AWS_INSTANCE_CNAME, AWS_ALIAS_DNS_NAME, AWS_INSTANCE_PORT, AWS_EC2_INSTANCE_ID, AWS_INIT_HEALTH_STATUS keys pass through verbatim as map string values on both sides — no casing/unit transform needed, it's a raw string map both in CFN and TF).
- instanceId (string, OPTIONAL in Cfn — CFN auto-generates a physical ID if omitted) -> ServiceDiscoveryInstanceConfig.instanceId (string, REQUIRED in TF aws provider). MISMATCH CONFIRMED: CFN prop is optional (readonly instanceId?: string, line 226); TF config field is required (readonly instanceId: string, line 24). The TF resource has no server-side auto-generation of this id, so when the CDK app relies on CfnInstance's optional instanceId (letting CloudFormation assign the logical-id-derived physical name), the converter must synthesize/supply an explicit instanceId value (e.g. derived from the CDK construct id or Names.uniqueId) since it cannot be left undefined in cdktf.
- serviceId (string, required, accepts either an ID or ARN per docs) -> ServiceDiscoveryInstanceConfig.serviceId (string, required). Same semantics; in the L2 constructs this is always sourced from the parent Service's serviceId, so on the TF side it should be wired to the service_discovery_service resource's id attribute.

TF-only fields (no CFN counterpart, do not affect the mapping): ServiceDiscoveryInstanceConfig also exposes optional meta arguments 'id' (optional, provider-managed/computed) and 'region' (optional, defaults to provider region), plus standard TerraformMetaArguments — none require a value from CfnInstance and can be left to defaults.

No unmappable CFN props: CfnInstance has no Tags, no other nested/complex sub-objects, and no attrArn/attrId CFN readonly attributes (unlike CfnPrivateDnsNamespace/CfnPublicDnsNamespace/CfnService; CfnInstance itself exposes no attr* outputs — only an instanceRef) — so nothing is dropped and nothing spins off into a second TF resource. The 'one Cfn -> multiple TF resources' caveat does not apply here; the four L2 wrapper files (alias-target-instance.ts, cname-instance.ts, ip-instance.ts, non-ip-instance.ts) are all pure convenience wrappers around the same single CfnInstance that just prefill different instanceAttributes keys (AWS_ALIAS_DNS_NAME for alias-target, AWS_INSTANCE_CNAME for cname, AWS_INSTANCE_IPV4/IPV6+PORT for ip, arbitrary custom attrs for non-ip) — they do not introduce any additional CFN resource types, so the TF mapping is the same single aws_service_discovery_instance for all four.
